--- title: "Vital Statistics" description: "Regularly updated charts tracking employment, business activity, housing, population, and crime in Waterloo Region." image: images/card.png # the link image, drawn by R/make_card.R draft: false # The page's last publish date, shown under the description as "Last updated". # /publish sets it to the day it publishes this page; there is no need to type it. date-modified: 2026-10-12 language: title-block-modified: "Last updated" # Quarto's label is "Modified"; this page only body-classes: vital-statistics # custom.scss rules a line under the subtitle # A page, not a post, so posts/_metadata.yml does not apply here: its # execute settings are repeated below so the page shows charts and not code. execute: echo: false warning: false message: false --- Looking for a handy overview of employment, business activity, housing, population, and crime in Waterloo Region? This Vital Statistics page is where to look. It contains a regularly updated collection of charts on the Region's health in each of these key areas, often with Ontario and Canada added for comparison. Most of the data used to produce these charts is updated monthly, so this page will be refreshed at least once a month to capture the latest statistics. The rental, population, and crime data is released annually, so those charts will only change once a year. The data in many of these charts will also be analyzed in more depth in regular posts. The population and crime charts include data for the entire Region, but for all other charts, only data for the Kitchener-Cambridge-Waterloo census metropolitan area (CMA) is available. The CMA covers the Region excluding Wellesley Township. Wellesley contains only 1.7% of the Region's population, so its exclusion from the data has no meaningful impact on the statistics in these charts. As such, the term "Region" is used throughout the charts on this page. All charts are interactive, so hovering over any line or bar shows a box with details of the underlying data point. See [Key terms](#key-terms) for definitions. Unless otherwise indicated, this legend applies to all charts on this page.

``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {#key-terms .callout-note collapse="true"} ## Key terms | Term | Definition | |------------------------------------|------------------------------------| | Active businesses | "Active businesses are those businesses that reported having one or more employees in a given month." (Statistics Canada, table 33-10-0270-01, footnote 4) | | Apartment | "all dwellings other than those described above, including structures commonly known as stacked townhouses, duplexes, triplexes, double duplexes and row duplexes." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption, "Apartment and Other") | | Average rent | "The rent refers to the actual amount tenants pay for their unit. No adjustments are made for the inclusion or exclusion of amenities and services." (CMHC, Methodology for Rental Market Survey) | | Condo | "an individual dwelling unit which is privately owned, but where the building and/or the land are collectively owned by all dwelling unit owners." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption, "Condominium") | | Crime Severity Index | "The Crime Severity Index (CSI) measures changes in the level of severity of crime in Canada from year to year. In the index, all crimes are assigned a weight based on their seriousness. The level of seriousness is based on actual sentences handed down by the courts in all provinces and territories. More serious crimes are assigned higher weights, less serious offences lower weights." "The crime severity index includes all Criminal Code violations including traffic, as well as drug violations and all Federal Statutes." (Statistics Canada, table 35-10-0026-01, footnotes 20 and 16) | | Employment | "Number of persons who, during the reference week, worked for pay or profit, or performed unpaid family work or had a job but were not at work due to own illness or disability, personal or family responsibilities, labour dispute, vacation, or other reason. Those persons on layoff and persons without work but who had a job to start at a definite date in the future are not considered employed." (Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0459-01, footnote 7) | | Homeowner | "a residence where the owner owns the dwelling and lot outright." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption) | | Housing starts | A start is "the beginning of construction work on a building. This is usually when the concrete has been poured for the whole of the footing around the structure or an equivalent stage where a basement will not be part of the structure." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption) | | Immigrant | "Immigrant refers to a person who is, or who has ever been, a permanent resident (landed immigrant). Such a person has been granted the right to live in Canada permanently by immigration authorities. Immigrants who have obtained Canadian citizenship by naturalization are included in this group." ([Statistics Canada](https://www23.statcan.gc.ca/imdb/p3Var.pl?Function=Unit&Id=85107)) | | Incidents | The number of incidents reported to a police service. Unreported crimes are therefore not included in this number. | | Interprovincial migration | "Interprovincial migration represents all movement from one province or territory to another involving a change in the usual place \[of\] residence." (Statistics Canada, Annual Demographic Estimates: Subprovincial Areas, Appendix A: Glossary) | | Intraprovincial migration | "Intraprovincial migration or subprovincial migration represents all movement from one region to another within the same province or territory involving a change of the usual place \[of\] residence." (Statistics Canada, Annual Demographic Estimates: Subprovincial Areas, Appendix A: Glossary) | | Labour force | "Number of civilian, non-institutionalized persons 15 years of age and over who, during the reference week, were employed or unemployed." (Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0459-01, footnote 6) | | Natural increase in population | "Variation of the population size over a given period as a result of the difference between the numbers of births and deaths." (Statistics Canada, Annual Demographic Estimates: Subprovincial Areas, Appendix A: Glossary) | | New Housing Price Index | "The New Housing Price Index (NHPI) is a monthly series that measures changes over time in the builders' selling prices of new residential houses, where detailed specifications pertaining to each house remain the same between two consecutive periods." "The index base period, for which the New Housing Price Index (NHPI) equals 100, is December 2016." (Statistics Canada, New Housing Price Index survey description; table 18-10-0205-01, footnote 3) | | Non-permanent resident | "A non-permanent resident refers to a person from another country with a usual place of residence in Canada and who has a work or study permit or who has claimed refugee status (asylum claimant, protected person or member of related groups). Family members living with work or study permit holders are also included unless these family members are already Canadian citizens, landed immigrants (permanent residents), or non-permanent residents themselves." (Statistics Canada, table 17-10-0153-01, footnote 13) | | Non-violent crime | "The non-violent crime severity index includes all non-violent Criminal Code violations including traffic, as well as drug violations and all Federal Statutes." (Statistics Canada, table 35-10-0026-01, footnote 19) | | Openings | "Opening businesses are businesses that transition from having no employees in the previous month to having at least one employee in the current month. These instances occur when a new, small firm begins, when a large firm opens a new establishment or when a seasonal firm re-opens." (Statistics Canada, table 33-10-0270-01, footnote 1) | | Participation rate | "The participation rate is the number of labour force participants expressed as a percentage of the population 15 years of age and over. The participation rate for a particular group (age, gender, marital status, etcetera.) is the number of labour force participants in that group expressed as a percentage of the population for that group." (Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0459-01, footnote 10) | | Regular beneficiaries | "The number of beneficiaries represents a count of persons who qualified for employment insurance benefits during the Labour Force Survey reference week, usually containing the 15th day of the month." "Includes people who receive regular income benefits whether or not they participate in one of three employment benefit programs, namely Skills Development Program, Job Creation Partnerships Program and Self-employment Program." (Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0454-01, footnotes 4 and 1) | | Rental | "a dwelling constructed for rental purposes, regardless of who finances the structure." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption) | | Row | "a 1-family dwelling unit in a row of 3 or more attached dwellings separated by a common or party wall extending from ground to roof." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption, "Row (Townhouse)") | | Same-sample rent change | "Percentage change in average rent provides an estimate of rent level movement by eliminating the compositional effects of new structures, conversions and survey sample rotation. The estimate is based on existing rental structures that were common to the survey sample for both the previous year and the current Rental Market Survey year." (CMHC, Methodology for Rental Market Survey) | | Semi-detached | "1 of 2 dwellings located side-by-side in a building, adjoining no other structure and separated by a common or party wall extending from ground to roof." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption) | | Single-detached | "a building containing 1 dwelling unit, which is completely separated on all sides from any other dwelling or structure." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption, "Single-Detached") | | Unemployment rate | "The unemployment rate is the number of unemployed persons expressed as a percentage of the labour force. The unemployment rate for a particular group (age, gender, marital status, etcetera.) is the number unemployed in that group expressed as a percentage of the labour force for that group." (Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0459-01, footnote 9) | | Vacancy rate | "A unit is considered vacant if, at the time of the survey, the unit is physically unoccupied and available for immediate rental." The survey covers "all row projects and apartment structures with three or more units" that are "privately initiated". (CMHC, Methodology for Rental Market Survey) | | Violent crime | "The violent crime severity index includes all Incident-based Uniform Crime Reporting Survey (UCR2) violent violations." from a monthly survey of about 65,000 households, and a CMA's share of that sample is small; "estimates are based on smaller sample sizes the more detailed the table becomes, which could result in The counts of openings and closures are not flagged in the months shown, so the net openings bars have no gaps. The chart's 12-month average also uses the year before the first month shown, and there the Region's openings for August 2020 are flagged E and not used, so no average can be worked out for July 2021 and the line starts in August 2021. (table 34-10-0292) | | **Population estimates are revised:** the latest year's population and components are preliminary and the two or three before it updated; each is revised as later data come in, the last when the next census is counted. (tables 17-10-0152, 17-10-0153, 17-10-0155) | | **Crime Severity Index and incident rates:** police-reported crime only; the previous year's figures are revised each year; the index weights were updated with 2022 data; and some older records were imputed from the aggregate survey. (tables 35-10-0026, 35-10-0177) | | **Railway police undercount, 2021 and 2022:** the "Other Federal Statutes" incidents the Canadian Pacific Railway Police reported for 2021 and 2022 "may be an undercount" and "should be interpreted with caution". (table 35-10-0177) | | **CMHC housing starts:** CMHC counts starts every month in census metropolitan areas and census agglomerations, the centres of 10,000 people or more; smaller places are counted only quarterly, by sample.
